Use paired, dataset-stratified user bootstrap: save each variant’s binary hit@10 for every validation user; resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical sampled indices across variants; recompute the four-category macro-average difference over 10,000 replicates. Report paired 95% intervals, category results, and discordant-user counts. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude candidate-sampling and training-seed uncertainty. Per-user pairing follows established [recommendation-evaluation guidance](https://tzin.bgu.ac.il/~shanigu/Publications/JMLRSurvey.pdf).

Predeclare four variants, checkpoint opportunities, selection rules, and comparisons. Four variants imply six all-pairs comparisons, or three comparisons against a designated baseline; use Holm-adjusted paired-test p-values or simultaneous bootstrap intervals. Checkpoints add selection opportunities: correcting only variant comparisons does not remove optimism from choosing each variant’s best epoch. Ordinary bootstrap intervals around selected checkpoints do not correct that selection bias. Prefer a predeclared final checkpoint for ablation comparisons, or disclose best-checkpoint results as exploratory. Repeated validation optimization can produce substantial [selection overfitting](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

A practical compute plan: preallocate the 43,200 GPU-second budget, including diagnostics and failed runs; use identical evaluation schedules and a minimum training allowance for every variant. Equal resource caps give the clearest ablation comparison. If pruning is necessary, predeclare successive-halving rungs and promotion counts, compare at matched resources, and label pruned runs accordingly. [Hyperband](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06560) supports resource allocation, not protection against validation reuse. Preserve seeds, splits, users, and candidates; stop at the budget cap rather than when significance appears. Without independent evaluation, conclusions remain validation-selected evidence.
